title: Microsoft Copilot: Agent Mode in PowerPoint builds presentations from Work IQ
summary: Hold: the licensing question treats Basic users' entitlement to Work IQ grounding as unresolved, although the cited Microsoft overview distinguishes Basic from Premium on this point. The roadmap facts, licence-assignment controls and Restricted Content Discovery controls are supported.

claims.claim: Agent Mode in Copilot in PowerPoint creates presentations based on a user's Work IQ.
claims.quote: Now with Agent Mode in Copilot in PowerPoint, you can create presentations based on your Work IQ.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the feature's default state on arrival.
claims.quote: Searched: "PowerPoint" "Work IQ" "default"; "Agent Mode" "PowerPoint" "admin" "enable". Read roadmap record, release-notes, copilot-overview and Work IQ overview. Found user creation steps, but no explicit arrival default for this feature.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Users > Active users > user > Licenses and Apps > Licenses reaches user licence assignment.
claims.quote: go to the Users > Active users page. ... Select the row of the user ... select Licenses and Apps. ... Expand the Licenses section, select the boxes for the licenses that you want to assign

claims.claim: Set-MgUserLicense with UserId, AddLicenses containing SkuId, and an empty RemoveLicenses array assigns a user licence.
claims.quote:
To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell.
Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.claim: At least License Administrator or User Administrator is required to assign licences.
claims.quote: You must be at least a License or User Administrator to assign licenses.

claims.claim: User licence assignment controls entitlement to the Work IQ grounding included with Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium).
claims.quote: Work IQ is included with Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium)

claims.claim: SharePoint admin center > Sites > Active sites > site > Settings > Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot reaches Restricted Content Discovery.
claims.quote: In the SharePoint admin center, expand Sites and select Active sites. ... Select the site you want to configure. ... Open the Settings tab, and then turn Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot on.

claims.claim: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true enables Restricted Content Discovery for a site.
claims.quote: Enable Restricted Content Discovery for a site ... Use PowerShell ... Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery requires the organisation to have a Microsoft Copilot licence.
claims.quote: Ensure your organization has a Microsoft Copilot license.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery requires SharePoint Advanced Management to be available.
claims.quote: You can configure Restricted Content Discovery if your organization is licensed for Copilot and has SharePoint Advanced Management available.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is a site-level control for SharePoint sites.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery is a site-level setting. ... You can only apply this feature to SharePoint sites. It's not supported for OneDrive sites.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery governs Microsoft Copilot discovery scenarios, including tenant-wide content discovery.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery affects organization-wide search experiences (SharePoint home, Office.com, Bing) and Microsoft Copilot discovery scenarios, including experiences that rely on tenant-wide content discovery.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery does not affect experiences operating on content already in use, such as an open document.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery doesn't affect experiences that operate on content that's already in use by the user, such as summarizing an open document.

claims.claim: Microsoft describes Restricted Content Discovery as a temporary governance control while access is reviewed.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery is designed as a temporary governance control that gives organizations time to review and right-size access while continuing their Copilot deployment.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery does not change permissions.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery doesn't change existing permissions. Users who already have access to content can continue to access that content directly.

claims.claim: By default, only SharePoint administrators can manage Restricted Content Discovery.
claims.quote: By default, only SharePoint administrators can manage Restricted Content Discovery.

claims.claim: Whether Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) users are entitled to the Work IQ grounding part remains an open licensing question.
claims.quote: Work IQ is included with Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) ... Copilot Chat (Basic) and Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) users don't have access to Microsoft Graph.
